uncited: All methods in this family share the core objective of mapping input image features to a set of 3D Gaussian parameters $\mathcal{G} = \{\mu, \Sigma, \alpha, c\}$ without per-scene gradient descent [Parent].
**Input Representation:** Inputs are typically one or more RGB images $I \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times 3}$.
Some methods require known camera poses $P$, while others (e.g., [Splatt3R](16423-splatt3r.md), [ZeroGS](16425-zerogs.md)) predict poses or operate on uncalibrated inputs [Parent].
**Feature Encoding:** A shared encoder (e.g., Vision Transformer, CNN) extracts multi-scale features from the input images.
Cross-attention or cost volumes are often used to aggregate multi-view information [Parent].
**Primitive Prediction:** A decoder head predicts Gaussian attributes.

**Differentiable Rendering:** The predicted Gaussians are rendered into target views using differentiable rasterization to compute reconstruction losses (e.g., L1, SSIM, LPIPS) for training the network [Parent].
**Generalization:** The network is trained on a large dataset of scenes to learn priors about geometry and appearance, allowing inference on unseen scenes [Parent].
*   Total output Gaussians: $N \cdot HW$ for $N$ input views, where $H$ and $W$ are image height and width.
